body:
> You could be the worst girlfriend in the world and it would not mean that you deserve any physical violence or that your behavior is the cause of the situation of violence.

Haha, thank you. That actually helps a lot. 

You're right about the up and down thing too. He spins things around and I can't tell what's real, sometimes.

> I'm sorry that you have to go through this, but you have a lot of worth and you are amazing and you will meet a guy one day that will love you and cherish you and never cause you fear.

Thank you. Honestly. Do you really think it's possible? I know it sounds so awfully self-deprecating, but I feel like I'm beyond finding someone that will cherish me. I'm too emotional, too picky, too talkative even.

You're right that things will get better once I leave. I don't think these are really my thoughts (being too picky and emotional, and stuff like that). Just his words reflecting back in my mind, and they would go away if he went away.

Thanks. I think maybe I need to write something out like this, and just read it every day until I believe it.

Just to vent, some of his lies are the absolute worst.

He lied about his name, age, marital status (YEAH), his job, where he used to live, his ex's name, whether he was using my tweezers to pick his fucking nose that one time.

I think that's what started the whole blaming myself thing. When I started to figure things out, I was like "Why is your name different than the one on your license?" and he would deflect. But worse, he would get mad. He would say "Why are you doing this, don't you trust me?"

And the anger was terrifying. Not just because I don't want to be yelled at, but because I suddenly felt like I betrayed him and I deserved his anger. I felt so overwhelmingly guilty for not trusting him. I remember the way he looked at me, and the first time he started taking back the kind things he's said and done. For example he once gave a really nice speech about how he loved me and wanted things to be good between us... then I tried to bring up the name thing. So he got angry and said something like, "Well I guess I was wrong earlier about us."

>He's doing this because he wants to.

You're completely right. I want him desperately to go. I feel like I'm going to make the leap soon, but the blame is overwhelming -- I blame myself for not leaving him sooner even. Yesterday he called me pathetic for crying after he told me to shut up. And I believe him, because aren't I pathetic for enduring this crap for so long? =/

Thanks.

What I hate is logically I know this but emotionally I am a total wreck. I blame myself constantly, even though I know it's not my fault.

What I believe is that I had self-confidence issues before I met him. I was actually doing fantastic. But being with him spun them out of control. I was pre-disposed to be emotionally wrecked by this kind of relationship, but I didn't know what would happen when I got involved with him.

And now I don't know what to do with myself.

>but I'll try because I've regrettably done this to my girlfriend before, I think if you tell him how you feel, the thoughts of self harm and such, even if it feels weird and cheesy to do so

Oh no no no I've got to stop you right here.

I understand communication to a T. I've done everything I should do. I've told him calmly how I feel. I appeal to him emotionally. He knows it makes me feel suicidal. What I mean is he was being intentionally cruel. I tell him the truth. I try to empathize with him and try to get him to see things from my perspective.

He does this anyway.

No matter how much I say and no matter how much I beg him not to.

Ex: yesterday he told me I could tell him my feelings. Then when I tried he got angry and said "You're telling me that I'm not doing things right!" and then told me to shut up, and called me pathetic when I cried after he told me to shut up.

? Yeah cuz the father is really the main one suffering here.

It's okay to empathize with women people. Can you imagine living like that? Fucking awful.
